Kaumārī
(‘feminine aspect of कुमार’)
------------------------------------------
Śakti or the Divine मोथेर् is said to have seven aspects known as ‘Sapta-mātṛkās’. कौमारी is one of them. She is the शक्ति or the feminine aspect of कुमार, also known as षण्मुख, सुब्रह्मण्य, कार्त्तिकेय, स्कन्द and by several other names.
Kaumārī is pictured as having six heads and twelve arms. Red in complexion and draped in red garments she rides on a peacock.
The twelve hands exhibit or hold varadamudrā (bestowal of boons), शक्ति (spear), patākā (banner), दण्ड (staff), घण्टा (bell), धनुस् (bow), बाण (arrow), kamala (lotus), kukkuṭa (cock), खेटक (shield), परशु (axe) and pātra (bowl).
She is one of the Śaktis or goddesses that emerged out of दुर्गा’s body during her fight with Śumbha and Niśumbha and their army.

Kaumodakī
------------------------------------------
Most of the gods of the Hindu pantheon are shown with weapons of various kinds. One of the common weapons is the गदा or mace.
The गदा of विष्णु is named ‘Kaumodakī’ since it gives ‘moda’ or happiness to ‘ku’ or the earth, by protecting it against the असुरस् (demons) and other evil forces.
It was fashioned out of the extremely strong bone of an asura called गदा. गदा gave up his body in deference to the wishes of ब्रह्मा, the ड़थेर् of च्रेअतिओन्. Then ब्रह्मा got it made by Viśvakarmā, the celestial engineer. It was then deposited with the god वरुण.
When कृष्ण got the Khāṇḍava forest consumed by अग्नि, with the help of अर्जुन, अग्नि requested वरुण to give it to कृष्ण as a sign of his gratitude to कृष्ण. Iconographical works show गदा as a female deity. Symbolically, it stands for cosmic intellect.
